# Sources — `legal-risk:disputes-and-legal-holds`

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-sources.py from sources/*.toml. Do not edit. -->

Check these before answering on anything they cover, and cite what you used. The use note on each one is binding: most of what a professional cites is free to read and not free to reproduce.

## Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

Administrative Office of the US Courts · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://www.uscourts.gov/forms-rules/current-rules-practice-procedure/federal-rules-civil-procedure>

**Authoritative for:** The duty to preserve and what follows from failing it — proportionality, the discovery conference, form of production, and the exclusive framework and intent threshold for sanctions over lost electronic evidence.

## General Records Schedules

US National Archives and Records Administration · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/grs>

**Authoritative for:** Minimum retention and disposition periods for common administrative record classes. Binding on federal agencies only — for a private company it is a defensible published baseline rather than law, which is still better than arguing from habit.

## The Sedona Principles and Commentary on Legal Holds

The Sedona Conference · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.thesedonaconference.org/publications>

**Authoritative for:** The operational standard of care for electronic discovery that federal courts routinely cite — when the duty to preserve triggers, the scope of a defensible hold, and custodian notice practice. Free to download, copyrighted, so cite rather than reproduce.
